candidate_name: Tongyeong Eco Power LNG Terminal (captive storage at Tongyeong CCGT)
sponsor_or_proposer: Tongyeong Eco Power Corp (HDC Group subsidiary); gas supply by Hanwha Energy
current_state: Phase 1 operating since Oct 2024: a single in-house 200,000 m3 LNG storage tank (reported as Korea's first power-generator-owned LNG storage tank) co-located with HDC's 1,012 MW Tongyeong combined-cycle plant. Phase 1 does NOT have its own import jetty/regasification — it shares the adjacent KOGAS-operated Tongyeong LNG terminal's regas facilities. Korean trade press reports a Phase 2 plan for 3 additional 200,000 m3 tanks plus a 520 t/hr regasification/send-out facility, which (if built) would make it a standalone import terminal; Phase 2 is in the MOTIE construction-plan approval stage, not yet under construction.
missing_threshold_elements: Borderline as a distinct GEM terminal: Phase 1 is a captive power-plant storage tank using KOGAS Tongyeong regasification (arguably part of/served by the existing GEM 'Tongyeong LNG Terminal' KOGAS infrastructure, T100000130315), not an independent import terminal. Phase 2 own-regas (the element that would make it standalone) has only a plan + pending approval, no construction start confirmed. Distinct-terminal status is contested; methodology judgment call on whether a power-gen captive storage tank sharing an adjacent operator's regas qualifies as a separate terminal.
watch_for: MOTIE construction-plan approval and/or construction start for Phase 2 (3x 200,000 m3 tanks + 520 t/hr regasification). If Phase 2 with its own send-out facilities is approved/started, stage as a new_terminal (FacilityType import, Owner Tongyeong Eco Power Corp, Parent HDC Group, Location Tongyeong Gyeongsangnam-do at Seongdong shipyard site) — entity_lookup returned not-found for 'Tongyeong Eco Power' so a new entity would be needed. Compare against existing GEM Tongyeong LNG Terminal (KOGAS) to avoid duplication.
notes: GEM tracks comparable power-gen captive terminals (KOMIPO Boryeong, KOSPO Hadong) as separate entries, which is why this is worth monitoring rather than dismissing; but those examples are cancelled. LNG Prime lead URL verified PASS (tokens 'Tongyeong','LNG storage'). Korean Phase-2 detail from energy-news.co.kr / e-platform.net trade press (not separately URL-verified — used as lead only). TotalEnergies supplies 600,000 t/yr LNG to Hanwha Energy under a 15-yr deal feeding this plant via the Tongyeong terminal.
